title: loc and iloc
setup:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("games.csv")
explanation: Back to the games! Every row has a label on the left, called the index: 0, 1, 2 and so on. loc picks rows and columns by label or by condition: df.loc[rows, columns]. For example, df.loc[df["price"] == 0, ["title", "genre"]] filters and picks columns in one step. iloc picks by position number instead, like a list: df.iloc[0] is the first row, and df.iloc[:3, :2] is the first 3 rows and first 2 columns. :3 means 'from the start up to (not including) 3'.

lines.explain: loc: pick by label or condition. Inside: rows, then columns.
Columns: only title and price. Result: Fortnite and Valorant.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: what will this print?
hints: iloc[0] is the row in position 0.

tasks.prompt: Fill in the blank to show the first 5 rows and the first 3 columns.
hints: The columns part :3 means 'up to 3'. Do the same for rows.

solution_lines.explain: Rows from the start up to 5, columns from the start up to 3.

tasks.prompt: Using loc, show the title and rating of RPG games.

solution_lines.explain: Rows: RPG games. Columns: title and rating. Elden Ring and The Witcher 3.

tasks.prompt: Using loc, show the title and genre of every free game.
hints: A free game has a price of 0.

solution_lines.explain: Free games: Fortnite, League of Legends and Valorant.

tasks.prompt: Predict first: what will this print?
hints: loc uses the row label, and labels start at 0.
Label 0 is Minecraft, 1 is Fortnite, so 2 is...

solution_lines.explain: Row label 2 is the third game, Super Mario Odyssey. The title column gives its name.

recap: You just learned loc (pick by label or condition: df.loc[rows, columns]) and iloc (pick by position, like df.iloc[:3, :2]).
